query: Consider the following context: Materials capable of withstanding extreme environments open promising opportunities for nuclear fusion reactors. In that context, which material can be used for interlayer materials between W and CuCrZr, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A molybdenum (Mo) interlayer placed between tungsten (W) and CuCrZr reduces thermal stresses and improves bonding strength for fusion-relevant conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Tungsten and CuCrZr components without interlayer bonding.
generation.intervention: Introduce a thin Mo interlayer (e.g., 10–30 µm) between W and CuCrZr before bonding.
generation.conditions: Repeated thermal cycling to elevated temperatures (e.g., up to 700 °C) representative of fusion reactor operation.
generation.structural_mediator: The Mo interlayer with intermediate thermal expansion properties.
generation.mechanism: The Mo interlayer decreases the thermal expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr, reducing interfacial stress and mitigating crack propagation under thermal shock.
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduced interfacial cracking and improved joint durability compared to W-CuCrZr bonds without an interlayer, leading to greater structural integrity under reactor-like thermal conditions.
generation.baseline: Joints formed by directly bonding W and CuCrZr, which are prone to interfacial cracks and bonding defects under repeated thermal loads.
generation.boundary: Performance gains may be limited at very high temperatures (> 1000 °C) or extended exposure times, where additional metallurgical changes (e.g., interdiffusion) could occur.
generation.uncertainty: Long-term effects under high neutron flux and extended service conditions remain uncertain without further experimental data.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of W-CuCrZr joints: one set with and one set without a 10–30 µm Mo interlayer. Subject these to repeated thermal cycles (room temperature to approximately 700 °C) to simulate reactor operating conditions.
measurements: Cross-sectional micrographs to quantify crack initiation and propagation at the interfaces
Tensile/shear strength of the joints before and after thermal cycling
Residual stress assessments (e.g., via X-ray diffraction)
Metallographic analysis of interdiffusion across the layers
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If there is no notable reduction in crack density or improvement in mechanical strength for joints with the Mo interlayer, or if the interlayer induces equally detrimental effects under these conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
